sourcedFrom: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 (2025)
cleanIntro: The Red Label III is a 20 gauge over-and-under with 28 or 30 inch barrels, made to Ruger's specifications by the Connecticut Shotgun Manufacturing Company. Its book covers only guns with a serial number starting RL20- or marked RED LABEL III; the earlier Red Label has its own book, and its choke tubes do not fit this gun. It opens with a top lever. The safety selector sits on top of the receiver, with a barrel selector in its middle: one red dot showing means the top barrel fires first, two red dots the bottom. Ruger's takedown is three pieces: the forearm, the barrels, and the receiver with the stock. That is all the takedown Ruger asks for routine cleaning. Keep the choke tubes screwed in while you clean.

steps.title: Safety to SAFE, top lever right, barrels down
steps.action: This guide is for a Red Label III only: Ruger's book covers guns with serial numbers starting RL20-, or marked RED LABEL III. An earlier Red Label is covered by a different book. Point the muzzles somewhere safe and keep your fingers out of the trigger guard. Move the safety selector back to SAFE, push the top lever all the way to the right and swing the barrels down to open the gun fully. Fired shells are thrown out, but live shells are only lifted a little: take every one out with your fingers. Opening the gun does not unload it.
steps.quote: You must remove live (unfired) cartridges manually!
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — To Unload, step 4, p.25
steps.warn: The selective ejector mechanism only ejects fired shells. It does not eject live ammunition.

steps.title: Look into both chambers, then close the empty gun
steps.action: With the gun open, look into the top chamber and the bottom chamber yourself and make sure both are empty. Put all the ammunition away from where you will clean. Then swing the barrels up until the gun locks shut: Ruger's takedown takes the forearm off a closed gun and opens it again after.
steps.quote: Check both chambers to be sure that the firearm is unloaded. Close the action by rotating the barrels upward until locked.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Disassembly Procedure, step 1, p.27

steps.title: Hold the forend latch button in, tip down gently
steps.action: Push in the forend latch button on the tip of the forearm and keep holding it in. While you hold it, pull the tip of the forearm down away from the barrels, slowly, only until you feel slight resistance. Stop there. Ruger warns that forcing it past that point can break it.
steps.quote: While pressing in the forend latch button, carefully pull down on the tip of the forearm until slight resistence is felt
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Assembling the Shotgun, step 2b, p.15
steps.warn: APPLICATION OF EXCESSIVE FORCE AT THIS POINT CAN RESULT IN BREAKAGE!

steps.title: Forearm forward and off
steps.action: Keep the tip of the forearm held away from the barrels and pull the forearm toward the muzzles. It comes off the barrels as one assembly. Once it is off, nothing but the closed action holds the barrels to the receiver, so handle the gun with both hands from here.
steps.quote: While holding the forearm tip away from the barrels, carefully pull the forend assembly toward the muzzle and remove it from the barrel assembly.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Assembling the Shotgun, step 2c, p.15

steps.title: Top lever right, open, lift the barrels out
steps.action: Hold the barrels firmly in one hand and the receiver in the other. Push the top lever all the way to the right and open the gun, swinging the muzzles down. Then lift the barrels out of the receiver: the trunnions in the receiver come out of their recesses at the front of the monoblock.
steps.quote: Securely holding the barrel assembly in one hand and the receiver assembly in your other hand, push the top lever all the way to the right and open the firearm, pivoting the muzzle end of the barrels downward
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Disassembly Procedure, step 3, p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench now: the forearm, the barrels, and the receiver with the stock. That is all the takedown Ruger's book gives for cleaning and maintenance. The stock stays on, and the trigger, safety and ejectors stay where they are. Leave the top lever where it is, pushed to the right: it has to be fully right for the barrels to go back on.
steps.quote: This completes the takedown required for all normal cleaning and maintenance purposes.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Disassembly Procedure, step 4, p.28

steps.title: Solvent patches, then dry patches
steps.action: Leave the choke tubes screwed in. With a proper cleaning rod, run a patch wet with solvent through each bore several times, then run dry patches through each bore until no residue is left. Ruger counts the chamber as part of the bore, so the chambers get the same treatment.
steps.quote: run a solvent-wetted patch through each bore several times. Then run dry patches through each bore to remove all traces of residue.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Care and Cleaning, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Brass brush only if the patches will not shift it
steps.action: If lead or plastic wad residue stays in a bore after patching, scrub that bore its full length with a brass-bristle brush wet with solvent. When the fouling has come loose, go back to solvent patches and then dry patches.
steps.quote: scrub the bore, full length, with a solvent-wetted brass-bristle brush
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Care and Cleaning, step 3, p.30

steps.title: Choke tubes stay in while you clean
steps.action: Do not take the choke tubes out to clean. Cleaning a barrel with its tube out pushes dirt and fouling into the choke threads, and then the tube may not seat and the threads can be damaged. If a tube does come out, do not fire the gun until it is back in, fully and tightly bottomed with the choke wrench. Use only Red Label III tubes: tubes for the earlier Red Label do not fit.
steps.quote: it is recommended that a choke tube be kept correctly tightened into bith barrels at all times, including during firing, storage, and cleaning.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Use of Screw-In Choke Tubes, p.20
steps.warn: Never fire the shotgun without the screw-in choke inserts in place.

steps.title: A very light film of oil on the monobloc and receiver
steps.action: Wipe the polished surfaces of the monobloc, the ejectors, and the inside of the receiver where the monobloc rests, then give them a very light film of gun oil. These are the surfaces that slide against each other every time the gun opens and closes. A film is enough; more only collects dirt.
steps.quote: The polished surfaces of the monobloc, ejectors, and inside surfaces of the receiver where the monobloc rests should be coated with a very light film of lubricating oil.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Care and Cleaning, step 4, p.30

steps.title: Lubricate where the forend iron meets the receiver
steps.action: Put a thin layer of a suitable lubricant on the area where the forend iron bears on the receiver. Do this at regular intervals, and every time the gun has been out in sand, dust, high humidity, condensation or water.
steps.quote: Lubricate the contact area of the forend iron and receiver with a thin layer of appropriate lubricant.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Periodic Maintenance, p.31

steps.title: Test any cleaner on a hidden spot first
steps.action: Before a cleaner touches the stock or the outside of the barrels and receiver, try it on a spot nobody will see and check it does not mark the finish. Ruger advises against caustic or acetone-based cleaners on this gun, and says never to use automotive or paint-stripping products on it.
steps.quote: NEVER USE AUTOMOTIVE OR PAINT STRIPPING PRODUCTS TO CLEAN YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Care and Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: Sparingly oiled cloth outside, oily patch before storage
steps.action: After the gun is back together, wipe the outside metal with a cloth that has only a little oil on it. If the gun is going into storage, swab each bore with an oily patch. Before you shoot it again, run a dry patch through both bores: oil left in a bore can obstruct it.
steps.quote: Swab the bores with an oily patch before storing the firearm. Do not apply excess oil.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Care and Cleaning, step 5, p.30
steps.warn: Firing a shotgun with oil, grease, or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the shotgun and serious injury to the shooter and those nearby.

steps.title: Long storage: centre the top lever
steps.action: If the gun is going away for a long time, centre the top lever to take the tension off its spring. With the barrels off, press the small button in the upper part of the receiver's breech face with a tool that will not mark it, and the lever returns to centre. Before the barrels go back on, push the top lever fully to the right again, into its locked-open position. Do not store the gun in a leather case or scabbard: leather holds moisture.
steps.quote: When storing the shotgun for an extended period, place the top lever in the center position to relieve spring tension.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® RED LABEL™ III — 12/2025 — Storage, p.32
steps.warn: Before reassembling the Red Label III shotgun, always ensure the top lever is fully pushed to the right into the locked-open position before installing the barrel assembly. Failure to do so will prevent proper assembly and may damage your firearm!

deepAbsentReason: Ruger's book ends at the field strip: after the forearm and barrels come off it says this completes the takedown required for all normal cleaning and maintenance, that further disassembly should only be undertaken by persons qualified in shotgun repair, and that the Red Label III should not be further disassembled by persons unqualified in shotgun repair (Disassembly and Reassembly Procedure, printed p.28).

cleaning.name: BORES
tasks: Solvent patch through each bore several times, chambers included
Dry patches until no residue is left
Brass brush with solvent only for lead or plastic residue the patches leave
Never fire the shotgun without the choke tubes in place

cleaning.name: MONOBLOC & RECEIVER
tasks: Monobloc, ejectors and the receiver seat wiped clean
A very light film of oil on those polished surfaces
A thin layer of lubricant where the forend iron meets the receiver

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Any cleaner tested on a hidden spot first
Never use automotive or paint-stripping products on the gun
Outside metal wiped with a sparingly oiled cloth
Oily patch through the bores before storage
Dry patch through both bores before the gun is fired again
Do not store the gun in a leather case or scabbard

reassembly: The forearm stays off until the barrels are on. Ruger says never try to attach the barrels to the receiver with the forearm on.
Push the top lever fully to the right, into its locked-open position. If it is not, the barrels will not go on properly and the gun can be damaged.

Hold the stock by the pistol grip in one hand and the barrels in the other. Lower the barrels into the receiver and engage the trunnions in the receiver with the recesses at the front of the monobloc.
Before you close it, make sure the small cams on the outside of the ejectors are in the ejector cam slots inside the front of the receiver. If they are not lined up, closing the gun can damage it.

Swing the muzzles up smartly so the monobloc seats in the receiver. The barrels are locked when the top lever returns to the centre. On a new gun the lever sits slightly right of centre, to allow for wear.
Put the rear of the forearm over the ends of the ejectors and swing the front of the forearm up until the forend latch button catches the hook under the lower barrel and the forearm snaps locked.
fncheck: Ruger asks for this check after every takedown, before any live firing. Both chambers empty, muzzles pointed somewhere safe. With the safety on SAFE, push the top lever right and open the gun, then try to push the safety forward to FIRE: it must stay on SAFE. Close the gun. With the safety still on SAFE, pull the trigger, move the barrel selector to its other side and pull again: no hammer should fall either time. Move the safety to FIRE and pull once: you should hear a hammer fall. Open the gun fully, switch the barrel selector, and close it again: the safety must have gone back to SAFE by itself. Move it to FIRE and pull again: you should hear the hammer fall. Ruger notes the gun resets between shots by inertia, so you may not be able to dry fire both barrels without opening it; that is normal. If any of this fails, stop using the gun and have a competent gunsmith or Ruger Customer Service look at it. Check the forearm is latched tight to the barrels.
